html:
The Yine, once called Piro, are an Arawakan people of the Urubamba and Ucayali rivers in the Amazon lowlands of Peru, with relatives, the Manchineri, in Brazil. They were known as river traders who travelled long distances by canoe, carrying goods between the foothills of the Inca lands and the lowland peoples.

Franciscan missions reached them in the 1600s and 1700s. During the rubber boom many Yine were forced to work for rubber barons. Their neighbours include the Matsigenka and Asháninka. The isolated Mashco Piro speak a related language.
